html:
The Dhirari, or Tirari, were an Aboriginal Australian people of the Far North of South Australia, on the east side of Kati Thanda, Lake Eyre, where Cooper Creek runs into the lake.

They are not the same people as the Diyari, though their language, now extinct, was a dialect of Diyari. Other neighbours were the Arabana across the lake and the Kuyani to the south. In 1866 Lutheran missionaries opened a mission at Killalpaninna on the lower Cooper, and it drew in many people of the region.
sum: The Dhirari, or Tirari, were an Aboriginal Australian people of the Far North of South Australia, on the east side of Kati Thanda, Lake Eyre, where Cooper Creek runs into the lake.
